title: Restart-safe mail storage readiness
summary: SMTP local delivery stores one authoritative RFC822 object, atomically commits recovery metadata and catalogue state, exposes idempotent mailbox projections, and fails closed when restart recovery finds orphaned or inconsistent storage state.
invariants: A local delivery is not reported durable until the RFC822 object has passed byte-for-byte readback and its recovery metadata has been committed.
SMTP metadata is committed through a temporary file and readback check; partial metadata cannot be treated as a successful delivery.
Storage Catalogue checkpoints are written to a temporary file and moved into place only after a non-empty checkpoint exists.
Mailbox membership is an idempotent projection over one stored object; retrying membership does not duplicate the RFC822 body or mailbox entry.
Mailbox consumers enumerate object identifiers and load the authoritative stored object rather than owning a second message copy.
Restart recovery reconstructs a fresh Storage Catalogue and SMTP store from disk before mailbox enumeration/reload.
LDAP Bind, message signing and durable storage do not confer MAIL_READ or EMAIL_SEND authority; access remains separately enforced by the platform authority.
Message reload requires a recovered Storage Catalogue object whose recorded size matches the stored RFC822 object.
Missing or incomplete recovery metadata is a storage failure; SMTP does not expose a partial reconstructed message.

qualification.note: dev7.2 adds a restart regression but does not claim a fresh autobuilder/live-host pass.
